newsitem.title: PERU: Peru survivors reach safety as snow abates.
newsitem.headline: Peru survivors reach safety as snow abates.

text.p: Survivors of a snowstorm that killed six people and trapped thousands of drivers high in the Peruvian Andes for three days began to reach safety on Monday, authorities said.
Soldiers found the bodies of six people, including three infants, who froze to death in their trapped cars.
The storm started to abate on Sunday, allowing traffic to reach towns along the winding highway 11,650 feet (3,500 metres) above sea level.
The first vehicles, including three buses carrying 120 people, ploughed through snow five feet (1.5 metres) deep in parts to get to safety, Civil Defence official Luis Barra told Reuters.
Many passengers had to be treated in hospital after spending days in freezing temperatures, but all were released hours later, hospital officials said.
Weather changes caused by the El Nino current warming surface waters in the Pacific Ocean have resulted in unusually cold temperatures this year in the Andes mountain range.
By midday on Monday, about 30 vehicles were still trapped on the mountain highway.
But meteorologists predicted the storm would die down by the end of the day and more vehicles were expected to arrive at nearby towns during the day.

The army flew food, blankets and medical supplies by helicopter to people still trapped on the snow-bound highway and planned to airlift the most seriously ill to Abancay, 380 miles (610 km) southeast of Lima.

Doctors and rescue teams reached the trapped vehicles late on Sunday. They said the people still stuck on the mountain road were no longer in danger despite the low temperatures and continuing snowfall.
The unusually strong storm affected the departments of Ayacucho, Apurimac and Arequipa, covering most highland roads with snow and making driving difficult in many areas.
